mainTopic: Whether a person gains atonement through שבח הקדש, רבי אלעזר's three questions to רבי יוחנן, and why some offerings have no fixed value
overview: The גמרא first finishes a question about the word "מעילתו" in the משנה. Its meaning depends on whether the ram he bought is worth the full קרן וחומש. Then רב מנשיא בר גדא asks whether an אשם bought from collected חומשים can bring atonement. That question leads to a more basic one: does שבח הקדש, a rise in an animal's value while he owns it, count toward the two-סלע אשם? Several proofs are pushed off. One ברייתא is shown to follow a תנא who counts שבח הקדש, with the extra דינר paid only as a rabbinic גזירה. But the גמרא then brings a ברייתא ruling that a ram worth one סלע when set aside does not work, even if it is worth two at atonement. רבי אלעזר asks three questions that רבי יוחנן reacts to: on שבח הקדש (answered from the offspring of a תודה), on whether live animals are pushed off (answered from the case of two partners), and on lambs becoming cheap. Finally, אביי and רבא challenge רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's reason why offerings of מחוסרי כפרה have no fixed value, and the גמרא leaves it as a קשיא.

steps.title: The latter case uses the word differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the סיפא of the משנה uses "מעילתו" for the איל אשם, while the רישא used it for the repayment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the latter clause calls the guilt-offering ram "his מעילה"!
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a question that started just before this point. In the רישא, the word "מעילתו" meant the repayment for what he took, but here in the סיפא the same word means the איל אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One word in one משנה seems to mean two different things. The גמרא wants to know why the משנה is not consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of the משנה
"His מעילה": what he owes because he misused הקדש
A ram brought as a guilt offering

phrases.english: The latter clause calls it
"his misuse" for the guilt-offering ram!

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵיפָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ לִ״מְעִילָתוֹ״ אֵיל אָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question about wording that began just before this point
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's use of the word "מעילתו"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word cannot mean repayment in one clause and the אשם in the next without a reason

steps.title: It depends on whether the ram covers the full repayment
steps.stepSummary: In the רישא the bigger ram is worth the קרן וחומש, so it is his repayment. In the סיפא it is not, so "מעילתו" refers to the איל אשם, and he adds a סלע and its חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the first clause, the bigger ram is worth the principal plus its fifth, so the משנה calls his repayment "his misuse." In the latter clause, the ram he bought is not worth the principal plus a fifth. So the משנה calls the guilt-offering ram "his misuse," and he brings with it a סלע and its fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the word changes because the facts change. What matters is whether the ram he bought is worth enough to pay back the קרן וחומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, the extra ram covers the full repayment, so that ram is "מעילתו." In the סיפא, the ram does not cover it, so the word points to the איל אשם. He then pays the קרן וחומש separately, as a סלע and its חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה
The principal amount plus an added fifth, paid for misusing הקדש
What he took, meaning the repayment for it
A silver coin

steps.whatToRemember: "מעילתו" points to the repayment when the ram is worth the full קרן וחומש. When it is not, "מעילתו" points to the איל אשם, and the repayment is paid separately.

phrases.english: The first clause, where he has
the bigger ram worth the principal and its fifth –
phrases.notes: "רובן" means the bigger of his two rams.

phrases.english: they call his repayment for what he took "his misuse."
The latter clause, where the ram
that he bought is not worth the principal and fifth –
it calls the guilt-offering ram "his misuse,"
and he brings with it a סלע and its fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא, דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ אַיִל רוּבָּן קֶרֶן וְחוּמְשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by their facts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה uses one word in two different ways for no reason
steps.terutzMaskana: The meaning follows whether the ram bought is worth the full קרן וחומש

steps.title: Can an אשם bought from collected fifths bring atonement?
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא בר גדא asks whether someone whose many חומשים add up to enough for an אשם can buy one with that money and gain atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא בר גדא asked: With collected fifths, what is the law? Can he gain atonement?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins here. Someone misused הקדש many times, and all the fifths he owes add up to the price of an אשם. Can he use that money for his אשם?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the אשם is brought with his own money, separate from what he repays. Here the אשם would come only from the extra fifths that piled up. The question is whether that kind of money works for atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: A collection of many fifths added together
Gains atonement

phrases.english: Rav Menashya bar Gadda raised a question:
With an accumulation of fifths,
phrases.notes: He misused הקדש several times, and the fifths he owes add up to two סלעים, the price of an אשם.

phrases.english: what is the law, can he gain atonement?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, a question about money for the אשם
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an אשם bought with accumulated חומשים can bring atonement

steps.title: One side: atonement may require his own effort
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out one side of the question. Atonement with a rise in a הקדש animal's value may work only because he took care of the animal. Here he put in no effort, so perhaps he gains no atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say: even if you say a person can gain atonement through an increase in הקדש's value, that is because he put in effort with it. But here, where he put in no effort, he does not gain atonement?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is hard by giving the side that says "no." This is setting up the dilemma, not giving the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא says 'אם תימצי לומר': even if we assume that a rise in a ram's value while he had it can count toward his אשם, the reason might be that he looked after the animal. Collected fifths just pile up without any work, so that reason would not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: "If you say": even if we accept a certain point
An increase in the value of consecrated property
He put in effort or trouble

steps.confusionAlert: This is only one side of the question, opened by "מי אמרינן" ("do we say..."). It is not yet the גמרא's ruling.

phrases.english: Do we say:
if you say
that a person gains atonement with an increase in הקדש's value –
that is because he put in effort with it,
but here, where he did not put in effort –
he does not gain atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind one side of the question in step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rule for atoning with an increase in הקדש's value depends on his effort, so that collected fifths would not work

steps.title: The other side: collected fifths were set aside, so maybe they work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the second side of the question. Even if שבח הקדש cannot bring atonement, collected חומשים might, because he set that money aside himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the opposite is true. Even if you say a person cannot gain atonement through an increase in the value of הקדש, that is because he never set that extra value aside. But these collected חומשים were set aside by him, so we can say he does gain atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving the other side of רב מנשיא בר גדא's question, the side that says he does gain atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 the key factor was effort: he put no work into the animal. Here the key factor is different. It is whether he himself set aside (הפריש) the money. A plain rise in value was never set aside by the owner, but each חומש was paid in by him, so his own act of setting aside may be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This introduces the other side of a question.
An increase in the value of something that belongs to הקדש.
He set it aside, meaning he designated it for הקדש.
A gathering of the extra fifths (חומשים) he paid, which together add up to a larger sum.

phrases.english: Or perhaps
if you will say
a person is not atoned through an increase in the value of הקדש,
that is because he did not set it aside;
phrases.notes: He set aside a cheaper ram. The extra value came on its own and was never set aside by him.

phrases.english: but this collection of fifths,
which he did set aside,
one can say he is atoned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the question that Step 4 began.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether setting aside the money (הפרשה) is enough to allow atonement through collected חומשים, even if שבח הקדש alone is not.

steps.title: The root question was already being asked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the basic question was already being asked: can a person gain atonement through שבח הקדש at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: For this was asked: can a person gain atonement through an increase in the value of הקדש, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that the basic question underneath רב מנשיא בר גדא's question was itself unresolved. This sets up the proofs that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מנשיא בר גדא's question depends on an earlier question that was never settled: does a rise in value count for atonement? The גמרא now turns to that root question and tries to settle it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them. This marks an open question among the חכמים.
Gains atonement, meaning his obligation to bring the קרבן is fulfilled.

phrases.english: For it was asked of them:
Is a person atoned through an increase in the value of הקדש,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points to the more basic question that Steps 4-5 depend on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an increase in the value of a הקדש animal count toward the required value of an אשם?

steps.title: Proof from the two rams bought with two סלעים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about two rams bought with two סלעים. It reads the case as a ram bought for one סלע that rose in value to two סלעים, which would prove that שבח הקדש brings atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: someone set aside two סלעים for an אשם and bought two rams with them. If one ram was worth two סלעים, it is brought as his אשם. The other ram grazes until it gets a blemish, then it is sold and its money goes to נדבה offerings. Isn't the case that he bought the ram for four דינרים (one סלע) and it rose in value to eight (two סלעים)? Then learn from this that a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from the משנה. It reads the case to mean that a cheap ram rose in value and was still used for the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two rams were bought with two סלעים, so each one should have cost about one סלע. If one ram is now worth two סלעים, it seems its value went up while he owned it. Since the משנה lets him bring it, the rise in value seems to count.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin worth four דינרים. An אשם must be worth at least two סלעים.
It grazes until it gets a blemish. Only then can it be sold, because it cannot simply lose its holiness.
Voluntary offerings brought for the community.
Isn't it that...? The גמרא uses this to suggest a reading that proves its point.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who sets aside two sela'im for an אשם
and bought two rams with them for an אשם,

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה אֶחָד מֵהֶן יָפֶה שְׁתֵּי סְלָעִים –
phrases.english: if one of them was worth two sela'im,
it is offered as his אשם,
and the second grazes until it gets a blemish,
and it is sold, and its money goes to voluntary offerings.
Is it not that he bought a ram for four,
phrases.notes: Four דינרים, which equals one סלע.

phrases.english: and it went up in value, so it is worth eight?
phrases.notes: Eight דינרים equals two סלעים, the amount an אשם needs.

phrases.english: So learn from it
that a person is atoned through an increase in the value of הקדש!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַמַּפְרִישׁ שְׁנֵי סְלָעִים לְאָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question raised in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of two rams bought with two סלעים, one of them now worth two סלעים.

steps.title: Rejected: the shepherd gave him a bargain
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The ram was really worth two סלעים when he bought it, and the shepherd simply sold it to him cheaply.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What case are we dealing with here? One where the shepherd lowered the price for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by explaining the case in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ram did not rise in value while he owned it. It was already worth two סלעים when he bought it, and he just got a good price. Since there was no increase in value, the משנה proves nothing about שבח הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? This introduces a narrower reading of a source.
He lowered the price.
The shepherd, meaning the seller of the ram.

phrases.english: No; what case are we dealing with here?
Where the shepherd lowered the price for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The גמרא keeps looking for an answer in the next steps.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ram rose in value, but it may have been worth two סלעים all along and bought at a discount.

steps.title: Proof from a ram that was fattened
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a ram bought for one סלע and fattened until it was worth two is valid. This seems to prove that שבח הקדש brings atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: someone bought a ram for one סלע, fattened it, and raised its value to two סלעים. It is valid. Learn from this that a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof, from a case where the ram's value clearly went up after it was bought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no one can say he got a bargain. The ram really was worth only one סלע and went up to two. Since it is valid, it seems a rise in value does count.

keyTerms.meaning: He fattened it.
Valid, meaning it may be brought as his אשם.

phrases.english: Come and hear: if he bought a ram for a sela,
and fattened it and brought its value up to two,
it is valid.
Learn from it
that a person is atoned through an increase in the value of הקדש!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof after the first one was rejected.
steps.raayaObject: That a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a ram bought for one סלע and fattened until it was worth two.

steps.title: Rejected: fattening cost him money
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. Fattening is different, because he spent his own money and in total paid eight דינרים, the full value of an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Fattening is different, because it cost him eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof, so it still needs a proof and keeps trying in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the price of the ram plus the cost of fattening it, he paid a full eight דינרים (two סלעים) out of his own pocket. So this is not a rise in value that came on its own. We still cannot prove that a rise in value without his spending counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different. This is used to set a case apart so it cannot serve as a proof.
It cost him, meaning he lost that money from his own pocket.

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs are rejected. A ram bought at a bargain, or a ram fattened at his own cost, is not a real case of שבח הקדש. The גמרא keeps looking for a proof in the next steps.

phrases.english: No; one who fattened it is different,
since it cost him eight.
phrases.notes: The one סלע he paid plus the cost of feeding come to eight דינרים, the full two סלעים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The גמרא tries another proof in the next step.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the fattening case he actually spent the full value himself, so it is not a free rise in value.

steps.title: A new proof from the second half of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's סיפא says a ram bought for one סלע that is now worth two is כשר, which seems to prove that שבח הקדש brings atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he bought a ram for one סלע and now it is worth two, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another proof from the same ברייתא. Its second half says that a ram bought for one סלע and now worth two is כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line does not mention fattening, so it sounds like the ram went up in value by itself. If a ram that went up in value by itself is good for an אשם that must be worth two סלעים, then the rise in value (שבח הקדש) counts toward his atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: A ram, the animal brought for an אשם
Valid; good to use for the קרבן
And now it is worth two (סלעים)

phrases.english: Come and hear: if he bought a ram for a סלע
and now it is worth two, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 10 pushed off the proof from the first half of the ברייתא. Now the גמרא tries its second half.
steps.raayaObject: That a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the ברייתא: a ram bought for a סלע that is now worth two is כשר

steps.title: This case too is about fattening
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: the סיפא is also talking about a ram that he fattened.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it means where he fattened it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by saying this second case is also one where he fattened the ram.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he fattened it, the rise in value came from his own money and not from שבח הקדש. So the case proves nothing, the same way step 10 pushed off the first proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; the same answer works in this case
He fattened it

phrases.english: Here too, it is where he fattened it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes off the proof of step 11 using the same fattening idea from step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the סיפא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rise in value may have come from fattening paid with his own money, not from שבח הקדש.

steps.title: Then the second half just repeats the first
steps.stepSummary: If the סיפא is also about fattening, it seems to be the same case as the רישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this is the same as the first half!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 12. If both halves are about fattening, why would the ברייתא say the same thing twice?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is not supposed to repeat itself for no reason. Reading the סיפא as fattening seems to leave it with nothing new to teach, so that reading looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your answer is true
That is the same as the first half
The first half of a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: If so, this is the same as the first clause!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the סיפא is also about fattening
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both halves describe fattening, the סיפא repeats the רישא and teaches nothing new.

steps.title: The two halves differ in how much he spent
steps.stepSummary: In the רישא he spent 4 + 4 = 8 דינרים. In the סיפא he spent 4 + 3, and the ram is worth 8.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first half is where he bought it for four and fattened it with another four, so it cost him eight. The second half is where he bought a ram for four and fattened it with three, and it is worth eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two halves are different cases. They differ in how much of the ram's value came from his own pocket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, his own spending covers the full eight דינרים. In the סיפא he spent only seven, but the ram is worth eight, so one דינר of value came from the ram growing in value by itself. So the סיפא is a new case, not a repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: He bought
He improved it; he raised its value (by fattening)
Eight (דינרים), which is two סלעים
The second half of a ברייתא or משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the numbers straight: one סלע is four דינרים, so two סלעים is eight. In the סיפא he paid only seven, so one דינר of the value came by itself.

phrases.english: The first clause is where he bought it for four
and raised its value with another four,
so that it cost him eight.
The latter clause is where he bought a ram for four
and raised its value with three, and it is worth eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both halves describe the same fattening case, so the סיפא is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is fully paid from his money (8). The סיפא is paid 7 from his money, plus one דינר of natural rise in value.

steps.title: Why pay a whole סלע if only one דינר is missing?
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says he must pay a סלע, but he only spent seven, so just one דינר is missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the ברייתא: 'He shall pay a סלע.' But he is only missing seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading of the סיפא using the ברייתא's own words, 'he shall pay a סלע.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 14 he spent seven דינרים, so he is short only one דינר of the needed eight. Paying a whole סלע (four דינרים) would be far too much, so the reading seems not to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (look at) the end of the source
He shall pay
Seven (דינרים)

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
'He shall pay a סלע' –
but he only spent seven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 14 using the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that in the סיפא he spent seven דינרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires a full סלע, but by this reading only one דינר is missing.

steps.title: 'Pay a סלע' means complete the סלע
steps.stepSummary: 'He shall pay' means he pays the rest of the סלע, the one missing דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he shall pay' mean? The completing of the סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the ברייתא's words differently. He does not pay a whole new סלע; he pays what completes the סלע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'pay a סלע' is read as 'finish paying the סלע.' He already put three דינרים toward it, so he adds one more. Now the numbers fit the case from step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: The completing payment of the סלע; the amount still missing from it

phrases.english: What is 'he shall pay'? The completion of the סלע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He shall pay a סלע' means a whole new סלע of four דינרים.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means paying what completes the סלע, which is one דינר.

steps.title: Paying one דינר does not create a two-סלע ram
steps.stepSummary: If שבח הקדש does not count, paying an extra דינר cannot help, because we need a ram worth two סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he holds that a person cannot gain atonement through שבח הקדש, what good is it when he gives the completion of the סלע? We need a ram worth two סלעים, and there isn't one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a deeper question about this whole reading of the סיפא. If the rise in value does not count, how can the ram be used at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the ram itself must be worth two סלעים. Handing over a separate דינר does not change what the ram is worth. So if the rise in value (שבח הקדש) does not count, this ram is not a two-סלע ram, and the ברייתא should not call it כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; this is his opinion
A person does not gain atonement
What does it help? What difference does it make?

steps.title: This תנא holds that שבח הקדש brings atonement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the תנא of this ברייתא really holds that a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he holds that a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 17 by saying that the תנא of this ברייתא holds that the rise in value of a הקדש animal does count toward a person's atonement. This is only one תנא's view. The next step challenges it, and step 21 asks for the final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ram in the סיפא counts as worth two סלעים only because its natural rise in value counts. So the ברייתא only makes sense if its תנא holds that שבח הקדש brings atonement. This tells us the view of one תנא. It is not yet the final הלכה, which the גמרא asks about in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; in truth (used to give the final answer)
He holds
A person gains atonement through the rise in value of הקדש

steps.whatToRemember: After several proofs were pushed off, the סיפא of the ברייתא shows that its תנא holds a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש. A ram that rose in value to two סלעים counts as a two-סלע ram.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that at least one תנא counts the rise in value toward an אשם. The ברייתא in step 22 gives the opposite ruling, so do not treat this as the final הלכה.

phrases.english: Actually, he holds:

phrases.english: a person can gain atonement through the rise in value of consecrated property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by saying this ברייתא's תנא counts שבח הקדש. The general question from step 6 is decided only in steps 21-22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תנא of this ברייתא holds that a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש. The general ruling is asked in step 21.

steps.title: Then why pay the missing דינר at all?
steps.stepSummary: If this תנא holds that a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש, the ram is already worth two סלעים, so the extra דינר should not be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should not have to give the rest of the סלע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the conclusion it just reached. If the rise in value counts, why does the ברייתא still make him pay the missing דינר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 the גמרא said this תנא holds that a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש. That means the ram's present value of two סלעים is enough. So the payment of the missing דינר from step 16 seems useless.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true

A coin worth four דינרים

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שבח הקדש counts, the ram is already worth two סלעים, so no extra payment should be needed.

steps.title: The extra payment is a rabbinic safeguard
steps.stepSummary: He pays the missing דינר only because of a גזירה, so that people will not think a ram worth less than two סלעים can serve as an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the reason he gives the rest of the סלע: it is a decree, so that people will not say that a ram worth less than two סלעים brings atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. By Torah law the ram is enough, and the extra דינר is a safeguard of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He only spent seven דינרים, so people might think a cheaper ram works for an אשם. The חכמים made him pay the missing דינר so nobody comes to that mistake. The הלכה that שבח הקדש counts stays in place for this תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree of the חכמים made to protect against a mistake
Lest people say; so that people will not think
A ram, the animal brought as an אשם
Brings atonement

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a rule in a ברייתא can come from a rabbinic safeguard and not from the basic Torah law.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to this ברייתא, שבח הקדש counts, and the missing דינר is a rabbinic safeguard.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?

steps.title: A ברייתא: the rise in value does not count
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a ram worth one סלע when it was set aside and two סלעים at the time of atonement does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if it was worth one סלע when he set it aside and two סלעים at the time of atonement, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. A ram that only reached two סלעים by going up in value does not work as an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is the ram's value when he set it aside. It was worth only one סלע then, so its later rise does not help. This shows that a person cannot gain atonement through שבח הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Setting aside an animal as a קרבן

He has not fulfilled his obligation

steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling is that a ram worth one סלע when set aside does not work as an אשם, even if it is worth two סלעים by the time it is brought.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with steps 18 and 20. That ברייתא's תנא does count the rise in value, but the הלכה given here is that it does not count.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is surprised at his student

steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן reacts to רבי אלעזר's question. He is surprised, because he had taught the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words suggest that he himself had stated a ruling on שבח הקדש. The גמרא will now check whether that is true and where he said it.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really state this?

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks what רבי יוחנן's surprise implies. Had he actually stated this halacha?

steps.title: Yes, he said it about a משנה on the תודה
steps.stepSummary: Yes, רבי יוחנן said it about a משנה: the offspring of a תודה, its substitute, and a replacement for a lost תודה are brought without the loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, and he said it about this, as we learned: the offspring of a תודה and its substitute, and also one who set aside his תודה, it was lost, and he set aside another in its place, do not need loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא confirms that רבי יוחנן did state this halacha and quotes the משנה he said it about. It is setting up how his ruling connects to that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a תודה is brought with loaves of bread. The משנה says the offspring, the substitute and the replacement animal do not need the loaves. רבי יוחנן's ruling on שבח הקדש was said about this משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A thanksgiving offering, normally brought with loaves of bread
Offspring; an animal born to the קרבן

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ruling on the offspring of a תודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חנניה reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the משנה's rule (the offspring of a תודה needs no loaves) applies only after the owner has gained atonement. Before atonement, the offspring does need loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנניה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The משנה only taught this about a case after atonement, because then the offspring does not need loaves. But before atonement, it does need loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: Here the גמרא spells out the actual ruling of רבי יוחנן that step 26 referred to. He limits the משנה about the offspring of a תודה to a case after the owner has already gained atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the offspring of a תודה is brought without loaves. רבי יוחנן says that holds only after the mother was already offered, when the owner's obligation is done. If the offspring is offered first, before atonement, it needs loaves, because it is now acting as the owner's real תודה.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about... (limits a source to a specific case)
Atonement, which the owner gets once his offering is brought
Offspring of a consecrated animal
Requires the loaves that go with a תודה

phrases.english: [Rav Chananya] in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.english: They taught this only after atonement,

phrases.english: because the offspring does not require loaves.
But before atonement – it requires loaves,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual wording of the ruling that step 26 said רבי יוחנן stated on the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The offspring of a תודה is exempt from loaves only after the owner's atonement. Before atonement, it requires loaves.

steps.title: So רבי יוחנן holds atonement through שבח הקדש works
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יוחנן's ruling, the גמרא concludes that he holds a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש. This answers רבי אלעזר's question from step 23.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that he holds a person can gain atonement through an increase of הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from רבי יוחנן's ruling. This closes the question רבי אלעזר asked back in step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offspring only exists because the holy mother gave birth. That makes it an "increase" of the הקדש, not a separate animal the owner set aside. Since רבי יוחנן lets the owner fulfill his תודה with it before atonement, he must hold that atonement can come through שבח הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: We see from this / evidently
He holds (this opinion)
Gains atonement
An increase or growth of something holy, like the offspring of a consecrated animal

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן holds a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש. We know this because the offspring of a תודה, offered before atonement, needs loaves and counts as the owner's תודה.

phrases.english: Evidently he holds
one can gain atonement through an increase of consecrated property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the underlying principle out of the ruling in step 27.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן holds that a person can gain atonement through שבח הקדש.

steps.title: Are live animals permanently pushed off?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks a new question: if a live consecrated animal was made unfit to be offered, is it pushed off forever, or can it become fit again?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked: Are live animals pushed off, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר opens a brand new question about consecrated animals. This sets up the next pattern, where רבי יוחנן reacts the same way he did in step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about an animal that was holy but could not be offered for a time. Once the reason goes away, can it go back on the altar? Or does being pushed off (דחוי) while still alive disqualify it for good?

keyTerms.meaning: Asked an open question (a dilemma)
Live animals
Are pushed off, meaning permanently rejected from being offered

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked:
Are live animals pushed off, or not?
phrases.notes: He means a live holy animal that became unfit to be offered. Does it stay pushed off for good?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, built the same way as רבי אלעזר's earlier question in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a live consecrated animal that was made unfit to be offered is permanently disqualified.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is surprised again
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן wonders how רבי אלעזר, after studying with him for so many years, never heard this הלכה from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This one has grown up among us for so many years, and he did not hear this הלכה from me!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן reacts with surprise to רבי אלעזר's question, just as he did in step 24. He is hinting that he has already ruled on this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not answer outright. His surprise suggests he once taught a clear ruling on this issue. That is what the גמרא will check next.

keyTerms.meaning: Grew up among us, meaning he studied with us
A legal ruling

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.english: So many years this one has grown up among us,
and he did not hear this halacha from me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רבי אלעזר's question with the same surprise as in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן hints that he already stated a ruling on whether live animals are pushed off.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן actually rule on this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן's surprise shows that he had stated a ruling on this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can we infer that רבי יוחנן said this ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether we can tell from רבי יוחנן's words that he had ruled on this issue. This sets up the answer, which brings his actual ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same move as step 25. The question looks for where רבי יוחנן's hidden ruling can be found.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference / it follows that
He said it

phrases.english: Does it follow that Rabbi Yochanan said it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether רבי יוחנן's surprised remark shows he had ruled on the matter.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where רבי יוחנן stated a ruling about whether live animals are pushed off.

steps.title: The case of the animal owned by two partners
steps.stepSummary: Yes, רבי יוחנן ruled on it. If one partner made his half of an animal holy, and then bought the other half and made it holy too, the animal is holy but cannot be offered. It can make a תמורה, and the תמורה is like it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as רבי יוחנן said: An animal owned by two partners, where one made his half holy, then bought the other half and made it holy: it is holy, but it is not offered. It makes a תמורה, and its תמורה is like it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes and brings רבי יוחנן's ruling about an animal made holy in two stages. This ruling is his answer to רבי אלעזר's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When only half the animal was holy, it could not be offered, so it was pushed off while alive. Even after the whole animal became holy, it still can never be offered. That shows רבי יוחנן holds live animals are pushed off for good. Its holiness is real, though, so it can make a תמורה, and that תמורה has the same status: holy, but not offered.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Partners
Made holy (consecrated)
It is holy, but it is not offered on the altar
A substitute animal that becomes holy when someone tries to swap it for a holy animal

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן holds that live animals are pushed off for good. An animal that could not be offered while it was only half-holy stays off the altar even after it becomes fully holy.
steps.confusionAlert: "Pushed off" does not mean the animal loses its holiness. It stays fully holy, and it can even make a תמורה. It just can never be brought on the altar.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case is the source for רבי יוחנן's view that בעלי חיים נדחין, and it answers רבי אלעזר's question.

phrases.english: Yes, as Rabbi Yochanan said:
An animal belonging to two partners,
one consecrated his half of it,
and then bought its other half and consecrated it –
it is holy, but it is not offered,
and it makes a substitute,
and its substitute is like it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 31 by showing where רבי יוחנן ruled on רבי אלעזר's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן ruled that a partly consecrated animal that later became fully holy can never be offered. This shows live animals are permanently pushed off.

steps.title: Three lessons learned from רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.stepSummary: From the partnership case, the גמרא learns three rules: a living animal can be pushed off forever, money-value holiness can push off, and pushing-off applies to money-value holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this: Learn that living animals can be pushed off for good. Learn that holiness of value can push off. And learn that pushing-off applies even to holiness of value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up what we learn from רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 32. This also answers רבי אלעזר's question from step 29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal could not be offered while only half of it was holy, and it stays unfit even after it becomes fully holy. So a living animal can be pushed off forever. Also, at first only its value was holy, since half an animal cannot be offered, and even that kind of holiness was enough to cause this pushing-off.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; a conclusion drawn from a source
Living animals can be pushed off (permanently made unfit to be offered)
Holiness of value: the animal is holy for its money worth, not as a קרבן itself
Being pushed off: becoming unfit with no way back

steps.whatToRemember: A living animal that became unfit to be offered stays unfit forever, even if the problem later goes away. This is true even when its holiness began as only holiness of value.
steps.confusionAlert: A pushed-off animal does not lose its holiness. It is still holy, and it can even make a תמורה. It just can never be offered.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the question from step 29: an animal that was pushed off while alive does not become fit again.

phrases.english: Learn from this three things:
Learn from it that living animals can be pushed off.
And learn from it that holiness of value pushes off.
And learn from it that there is pushing-off with value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the halachic lessons out of רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 32.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בעלי חיים נדחין; קדושת דמים מדחה; יש דיחוי בדמים.

steps.title: What if lambs become cheap everywhere?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks whether a ram worth less than two סלעים may be brought as an אשם when no ram anywhere is worth that much.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked: If lambs became cheap all over the world, what is the law? Do we say the requirement is 'your choicest vows,' and that is fulfilled? Or perhaps the requirement is 'silver by shekels,' and that is missing?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks a new question. The Torah requires an אשם to be worth two silver shekels, so what happens if prices fall and no ram is worth that much?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sides. If the main rule is to bring the best animal you can (מבחר נדריכם), the best ram available is fine. But if the rule is a fixed price (כסף שקלים), a cheaper ram does not count, even if no better one exists.

keyTerms.meaning: Became cheap; prices dropped
"Your choicest vows": the requirement to bring the best
"Silver by shekels": the fixed value of an אשם (two shekels)
Guilt offering, a ram that must be worth two silver shekels

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked:
If lambs became cheap in the world, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means an אשם ram, which must be worth two סלעים, when no ram anywhere is worth that much.

phrases.english: Do we say we need "your choicest vows,"
and that is present,
or perhaps we need "silver by shekels,"
and that is missing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his earlier question was answered, רבי אלעזר asks a new one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a fixed value of two סלעים required for an אשם even when no such ram exists, or is the best available ram enough?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says he never heard this הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that in all his years in the בית המדרש he never heard a ruling on this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: For how many years have we grown up in the study hall, and we did not hear this הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן responds that he has no tradition about this question. This sets up the גמרא's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words suggest that no answer to רבי אלעזר's question had ever been taught. The גמרא will now test whether that is really true.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall
We grew up (spent our years)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
How many years have we grown up in the study hall
and we did not hear this הלכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כַּמָּה שָׁנִים גָּדַלְנוּ בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן reacts to רבי אלעזר's question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן claims no ruling on this question was ever heard.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן himself taught a related teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי יוחנן quoted רבי שמעון בן יוחאי that the Torah gave no fixed price for the offerings of מחוסרי כפרה, because lambs might become cheap. That shows a fixed price can leave a person stuck, so the answer was known.
steps.simpleTranslation: And was it not heard? But רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: Why did the Torah not set a fixed price for the offerings of people still lacking atonement? Because lambs might become cheap, and they would have no way to eat holy food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's claim that he never heard this הלכה. He himself passed on a teaching that answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי explained that the Torah did not fix a price for these offerings, because if prices fell the people could never bring them. That implies that where the Torah does fix a price, as for an אשם, a cheaper animal cannot be used. So רבי אלעזר's question already has an answer that רבי יוחנן knew.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed amount or price
People who still need an offering to finish becoming pure, such as a זב or a מצורע
A remedy; a way to fix the situation
Holy food from offerings

phrases.english: And was it not heard?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נָתְנָה תּוֹרָה קִצְבָה
phrases.english: Why did the Torah not give a fixed price
for those lacking atonement?
phrases.notes: These are people like a זב or מצורע, who must bring an offering before they may eat holy food.

phrases.english: Because lambs might become cheap,
and they would have no remedy to eat holy food.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's claim in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that he never heard this הלכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own quoted teaching implies that a fixed Torah price cannot be lowered when lambs become cheap, so the answer was known to him.

steps.title: He meant: we never taught it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבי יוחנן's words: he did not mean he never heard it, but that he never taught it in the study hall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: We did not teach this הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing what רבי יוחנן meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן did know the idea, so his complaint must be that this הלכה was never taught openly in the study hall. That way the teaching from רבי שמעון בן יוחאי no longer contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead; read the statement this way
We taught

phrases.english: Say: we did not teach this הלכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן said he never heard the הלכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן meant that he never taught it in the study hall.

steps.title: But his student reviewed everything with him every month
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי זירא בר אדא reviewed his learning before רבי יוחנן every thirty days, so everything was taught again and again.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי זירא בר אדא reviewed his learning before him every thirty days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from step 37.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a student went over all his learning in front of רבי יוחנן every month, then this הלכה was taught regularly. So 'we did not teach it' also seems untrue.

keyTerms.meaning: Reviews his learning
Thirty days
In front of him

phrases.english: But Rabbi Zeira bar Adda
would review his learning
every thirty days before him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי זֵירָא בַּר אַדָּא מַהְדַּר תַּלְמוּדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי יוחנן never taught this הלכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Monthly review before רבי יוחנן means all his teachings, including this one, were taught often.

steps.title: He meant: no one ever asked us this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן meant this question was never asked of him in the study hall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: This הלכה was never asked of us in the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final reading of רבי יוחנן's words, which settles both challenges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching was known and reviewed, but nobody had ever brought this practical question to רבי יוחנן. So his surprise was about the question being new to the study hall, not about the answer being unknown.

keyTerms.meaning: Was asked; was requested
From us (of us)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's surprise does not mean the answer was unknown. The idea from רבי שמעון בן יוחאי was already taught; nobody had ever asked this question directly.

phrases.english: Say: this הלכה was not asked
of us in the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא לֹא נִתְבַּקְּשָׁה הֲלָכָה זוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the statement a second time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן meant he never taught the הלכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן meant the question was never asked of him in the study hall.

steps.title: Back to the statement: why there is no fixed value for offerings of מחוסרי כפרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the teaching of רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: the Torah set no fixed value for the offerings of מחוסרי כפרה. If it had, lambs might drop in price, and these people would have no way to become fit to eat קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: Why did the Torah not set a fixed value for the offerings of people who still need atonement? Because lambs might become cheap, and then they would have no way to eat holy food.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is now looking closely at a statement it quoted earlier in passing. It quotes the statement in full so it can analyze it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some offerings have a fixed minimum value set by the Torah. For מחוסרי כפרה there is none. The reason is practical. If prices fell below a fixed amount, no lamb would be worth enough, and the person could never finish his process and eat קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to look at a statement quoted earlier
A fixed set value or amount
People who are already purified but still must bring an offering before they may eat holy food
A remedy or way out
Holy sacrificial food

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new teaching. The גמרא already used this statement back in Step 36. Here it comes back to the statement itself in order to question its reasoning.

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
For what reason was no fixed value given
for those lacking atonement?
Lest lambs become cheap,
and they would have no remedy to eat sacrificial food.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the statement quoted in Step 36 so its reasoning can be analyzed directly
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no fixed value for the offerings of מחוסרי כפרה, so a drop in lamb prices will never leave them unable to eat קדשים.

steps.title: אביי: then a regular חטאת should have a fixed value
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the reason. A חטאת brought for eating forbidden fat is only for atonement. It does not permit eating קדשים. So by this reasoning, it should have a fixed value.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: If so, a sin offering for eating forbidden fat should be given a fixed value. It comes for atonement, not to let someone eat holy food!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the reason רבי שמעון בן יוחאי gave. He points to an offering where that reason does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason was: no fixed value, so that a person won't be blocked from eating קדשים. A חטאת חלב has nothing to do with eating קדשים. It only atones. So the worry doesn't apply, and the Torah should have set a fixed value for it. Yet it did not.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it: a strong challenge to a statement
'But now, if so': if your reason is right, then this other result should follow
A sin offering brought for accidentally eating forbidden fat (a regular חטאת)
To be permitted

phrases.english: Abaye objects to this:
If that is so,
a sin offering for forbidden fat should be given a fixed value,
since it comes for atonement
and not to become permitted to eat sacrificial food!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 40
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי for why there is no fixed value
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'no fixed value' exists only so that a person can eat קדשים, then an offering that does not permit eating קדשים (חטאת חלב) should have a fixed value. It does not.

steps.title: רבא: then אשם נזיר should have a fixed value
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a similar challenge from the אשם of an impure נזיר. That offering permits nothing at all. רבי יוחנן himself, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, said so. So it should have a fixed value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: If so, the guilt offering of a נזיר should have a fixed value, since it comes for nothing. As רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: There is no offering that comes for nothing except the guilt offering of a נזיר alone!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a second challenge of the same kind. He backs it up with another statement from the very same רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An impure נזיר becomes pure through the sprinkling, not through his אשם. So the אשם does not make anything permitted for him. Since it never lets him eat קדשים, the reason for having no fixed value doesn't apply. The challenge is extra strong because רבי שמעון בן יוחאי himself said this offering 'comes for nothing.'

keyTerms.meaning: The guilt offering brought by a נזיר who became impure
For nothing: it does not make anything permitted
Alone, only

steps.whyThisMatters: רבא uses רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's own words against his reason. That makes the difficulty very hard to answer.

phrases.english: Rava objects to this:
If that is so,
the guilt offering of a nazirite should have a fixed value,
since it comes for nothing,
as Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא בָּא לְבַטָּלָה,
phrases.english: There is nothing that comes for nothing,
except the guilt offering of a nazirite alone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge of the same kind as אביי's, from a different offering
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי for why there is no fixed value
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אשם נזיר permits nothing, as רבי שמעון בן יוחאי himself says. So the worry about not being able to eat קדשים doesn't apply, and it should have a fixed value. It does not.

steps.title: The challenges stand: it is difficult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that the challenges of אביי and רבא are not answered. The reason of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי remains difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion by saying the challenges have no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קשיא here means the question stands unresolved. The גמרא does not say the statement is thrown out completely, the way it would with תיובתא. It simply admits the reason does not fit every offering.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is difficult': the challenge remains unanswered, without fully rejecting the statement

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי explained 'no fixed value' as a way to keep מחוסרי כפרה from getting stuck. אביי (חטאת חלב) and רבא (אשם נזיר) showed offerings with no fixed value even though they never permit eating קדשים. The גמרא leaves this as an unanswered קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse קשיא with תיובתא. קשיא leaves the question open. It does not declare the statement disproven.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenges of Steps 41 and 42 without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenges of אביי and רבא to the reason of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי remain unanswered.
